learning_objective: 🎯 Master the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, calculate HCF and LCM, and prove the irrationality of numbers like √2 and √3!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every composite number can be expressed (factorized) as a product of prime numbers, and this factorization is unique, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.
HCF is the product of the smallest power of each common prime factor. LCM is the product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.
For any two positive integers 'a' and 'b', HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b. This is a very useful formula to find one value if the other three are known!

We use the 'Method of Contradiction' to prove numbers like √2, √3, or √5 are irrational. We first assume they are rational (can be written as a/b where a and b are co-prime), and then prove our assumption mathematically wrong.

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ The Prime Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Pick your birth year (e.g., 2010). Try to break it down entirely into prime numbers (Prime Factorization). See how many unique prime blocks make up your birth year!

exam_tips: 📌 Questions asking to prove '√3 is irrational' are almost guaranteed in board exams. Practice the exact steps of the contradiction method.
📌 Always check if the fractions you assume in contradiction proofs (a/b) are stated as 'co-prime'.
📌 Remember the formula: HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers. This only works for TWO numbers, not three!
quick_recap: ⭐ The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
⭐ Co-prime numbers are two numbers that have only 1 as their common factor.
⭐ A rational number's decimal expansion is either terminating or non-terminating repeating. An irrational number's decimal expansion is non-terminating non-repeating.
